standard_prerequisites.name: The self intersection of the diagonal computed by the Gysin map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Chow Homology, the lemma expressing the intersection product of the diagonal with itself through the Gysin map and the lemma identifying the Gysin map with capping by the top Chern class of the normal sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the identification of the self intersection of the diagonal with the top Chern class of the tangent sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The conormal sheaf of the diagonal is the sheaf of differentials
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, the lemma identifying the conormal sheaf of the diagonal with the sheaf of differentials
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the normal sheaf of the diagonal with the tangent sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pairing with the class of the diagonal through the degree map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma relating degrees of cycles to pairings of cycle classes, the lemmas on the pushforward of the unit and on pushforwards, and the lemma describing the class of the diagonal in the Kunneth decomposition
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes the self intersection through the degree map and the Kunneth components of the class of the diagonal.

core_obligations: The Chern class computation (proof lines 3541-3555): the self intersection of the diagonal is the pushforward along the diagonal of the Gysin pullback of the diagonal along itself, and since the pushforward preserves degrees of zero cycles it suffices to compute the degree of that pullback, which is given by capping with the top Chern class of the normal sheaf of the diagonal; the conormal sheaf of the diagonal is the sheaf of differentials, so the normal sheaf is the tangent sheaf.

The cohomological computation (proof lines 3557-3588): rewriting the degree of the intersection product through the degree map gives a chain of equalities using the projection formula and the pushforward of the unit, reducing to the pairing on the scheme of the pullback along the diagonal of the class of the diagonal; writing that class in its Kunneth decomposition and using that the pullback along the diagonal is given by the cup product, the pairing becomes an alternating sum of the Betti numbers, which is the stated Euler characteristic.
proof_roadmap: Compute the self intersection of the diagonal by capping with the top Chern class of the tangent sheaf.
Rewrite the same intersection product through the degree map.
Use the Kunneth decomposition of the diagonal to identify it with the Euler characteristic.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a nonempty equidimensional smooth projective scheme the alternating sum of the Betti numbers equals the degree of the self intersection of the diagonal and equals the degree of the top Chern class of the tangent sheaf (statement lines 3537-3544). The proof (proof lines 3545-3588) computes the self intersection through the Gysin map and the conormal sheaf of the diagonal, and through the degree map and the Kunneth decomposition of the diagonal class. H3: two independent computations of the same invariant, written out in full.
